duas: (How perfect He is, (The One) Whom the thunder declares His perfection with His praise, as do the angles out of fear of Him.)

title: Some invocations for rain
duas: (O Allah, send upon us helpful, wholesome and healthy rain, beneficial not harmful rain, now, not later.)
(O Allah, relieve us, O Allah, relieve us, O Allah, relieve us.)
(O Allah, provide water for Your servants and Your cattle, spread out Your mercy and resurrect Your dead land.)

title: Invocation for when it rains
duas: (O Allah, may it be a beneficial rain cloud.)

title: Supplication after it rains
duas: (We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah.)

title: Invocation for the withholding of the rain
duas: (O Allah, let the rain fall around us and not upon us, O Allah, (let it fall) on the pastures, hills, valleys and the roots of trees.)

title: Invocation for sighting the new moon
duas: (Allah is the greatest. O Allah, let the crescent loom above us in safety, faith, peace, and Islam, and in agreement with all that You love and pleases You. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.)

title: Invocations for breaking the fast
duas: (The thirst has gone and the veins are quenched, and reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.)
(O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy which envelopes all things, that You forgive me.)

title: Invocations before eating
duas: (When you are about to eat, you should say:(Bismil-lah.)and if you forget to say it before starting, then you should say (when you remember):In the name of Allah in it’s beginning and end.)
(Whomever Allah feeds, should say:(O Allah, bless it for us and feed us better than it.) and whomever Allah gives milk to drink should say:(O Allah, bless it for usand give us more of it.))

title: Invocations after eating
duas: (All praise is for Allah who fed me this and provided it for me without any might nor power from myself.)

(Allah be praised with an abundant beautiful blessed praise, a never-ending praise, a praise which we will never bid farewell to and an indispensable praise, He is our Lord.)(There are other views as regards to the under

title: A dinner guest's invocation for his host
duas: (O Allah, bless for them, that which You have provided them, forgive them and have mercy upon them.)

title: Invocation for someone who gives you drink or offers it to you
duas: (O Allah, feed him who fed me, and provide with drink him who provided me with drink.)

title: Invocation for a family who invites you to break your fast with them
duas: (May the fasting break their fast in your home, and may the dutiful and pious eat your food, and may the angles send prayers upon you.)

title: Invocation for someone who offers you food when you are fasting, which you decline
What to say when you are fasting and someone is rude to you
duas: (I am fasting, I am fasting.)

title: Invocation for when you see the first dates of the season
duas: (O Allah, bless our fruit for us, bless our town for us, bless our saAA for us and bless our mudd for us.)(A saAA is equivalent to four mudds and a mudd is equivalent to a dry measure of an average man’s two palms.)

title: Invocation for sneezing
duas: (When one of you sneezes he should say:(All praise if for Allah.) and his brother or companion should say to him: (May Allah have mercy upon you.) and he (i.e. the one who sneezed) replies back to him:(May Allah guide yo

title: What to say to the disbeliever if he sneezes and praises Allah
duas: (May Allah guide you and rectify your condition.)

title: Invocation for the groom
duas: (May Allah bless for you (your spouse) and bless you, and may He unite both of you in goodness.)

title: The groom’s supplication on the wedding night or when buying an animal
duas: (when you marry a woman or buy a maidservant, you should say:(O Allah, I ask You for the goodness within her and the goodness that you have made her inclined towards, and I take refuge with You from the evil within her a

title: Invocation to be recited before intercourse
duas: (In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep the devil away from us and keep the devil away from what you have blessed us with.)

title: Invocation for anger
duas: (I take refuge with Allah from the accursed devil.)

title: What to say if you see someone afflicted by misfortune
duas: (All praise is for Allah Who saved me from that which He tested you with and Who most certainly favoured me over much of His creation.)

title: What to say while sitting in an assembly
duas: (Ibn AAumar said: It would be counted that the Messenger of Allah would say one hundred times at any one sitting before getting up: (O my Lord, forgive me and turn towards me (to accept my repentance). Verily You are The

title: The Expiation of Assembly - Kaffaratul-Majlis
duas: (How perfect You are O Allah, and I praise You. I bear witness that None has the right to be worshipped except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.)

title: Vocation for someone who says: May Allah forgive you
duas: (AAabdullah Ibn Sarjis said: ‘I went to see the Prophet and ate from his food and then said to him: (May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah.) he replied: (and you.))

title: Invocation for someone who does good to you
duas: (If someone does you a favour and you say: (May Allah reward you with goodness.) then you have indeed excelled in praising him.)

title: Invocation for Allah's protection from the False Messiah
duas: (Dajjal: among the great signs of the last hour and the greatest trials to befall mankind, which every Prophet has warned about. Most of mankind will folow him. He will appear from Asbahan, Iran at the time when Muslims

title: Invocation for someone who tells you I love you for the sake of Allah
duas: (May He, for whom you have loved me, love you.)

title: Invocation for someone who offers you a share of his wealth
duas: (May Allah bless for you, your family and wealth.)

title: Invocation (upon receipt of the loan) for someone who lends you money
duas: (May Allah bless for you, your family and wealth. Surely commendation and payment are the reward for a loan.)

title: Invocation for fear of Shirk
duas: (shirk: to associate others with Allah in those things which are specific to Him. This can occur in (1) belief, e.g. to believe that other than Allah has the power to benefit or harm, (2) speech, e.g. to swear by other t

title: Invocation for someone who tells you: May Allah bless you
duas: (Aaishah reported that the Messenger of Allah was given a sheep and he ordered for it’s distribution. When the servant would come back (from distributing it), AAaishah would ask: ‘What did they say?’, he replied: They wo

title: Invocation against evil portent
duas: (This supplication is used whenever one initially thinks a casual event or occurrence to foretell good or evil, using it as a basis to determine which action he should undertake, but he then denounces such a link, relies

title: Invocation for riding in a vehicle or on an animal
duas: (In the name of Allah and all praise is for Allah. How perfect He is, the One Who has placed this (transport) at our service and we ourselves would not have been capable of that, and to our Lord is our final destiny. All

title: Invocation for traveling
duas: (Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, How perfect He is, The One Who has placed this (transport) at our service, and we ourselves would not have been capable of that, and to our Lord is ou

title: Invocation for entering a town or city
duas: (O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all that they envelop, Lord of the seven earths and all that they carry, Lord of the devils and all whom they misguide, Lord of the winds and all whom they whisk away. I ask You fo

title: Invocation for entering a market
duas: (None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner, to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is living and does not die. In His hand is all good and He is o

title: Invocation for when your vehicle or mount begins to fail
duas: (In the name of Allah.)

title: The traveler's invocation for the one he leaves behind
duas: (I place you in the trust of Allah, whose trust is never misplaced.)

title: The resident's invocations for the traveler
duas: (I place your religion, your faithfulness and the ends of your deeds in the trust of Allah.)

(May Allah endow you with taqwa, forgive your sins and facilitate all good for you, wherever you be.)(taqwa: a comprehensive term which refers to all good actions and obedience i.e. performing the commanded actions and a

title: Glorifying and magnifying Allah on the journey
duas: Jabir said: Whenever we went up a hill we would say Allaahu 'Akber (Allah is the Most Great) and when we descended we would say Subhaanallaah (Glory is to Allah)

title: The traveler's invocation at dawn
duas: (May a witness, be witness to our praise of Allah for His favours and bounties upon us. Our Lord, protect us, show favour on us and deliver us from every evil. I take refuge in Allah from the fire.)

title: Invocation for a layover (stopping along the way) on the journey
duas: (I take refuge in Allah’s perfect words from the evil that He has created.)

title: What to say upon returning from a Journey
duas: (Ibn AAumar reported that the Messenger of Allah on return from a battle or from performing the pilgrimage would say at every high point: (Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest.) and then he

title: What to say if something happens to please you or to displease you

title: The excellence of asking for Allah's blessings upon the Prophet pbuh
duas: (The Prophet (PBUH) said: ‘Whoever sends a prayer upon me, Allah sends ten upon him.)
(He (PBUH) also said: ‘Do not take my grave as a place of habitual ceremony. Send prayers upon me, for verily your prayers reach me wherever you are.)
(He (PBUH) also said: ‘A miser is one whom when I am mentioned to him, fails to send prayers upon me.)
The Prophet [PBUH] said:'Indeed Allah has angels who roam the earth and they convey to me the greetings (or prayers of peace) of my 'Ummah (nation).
The Prophet [PBUH] said: 'No one sends greetings (or prayers of peace) upon me but Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greetings

title: Spreading the greetings of Salam (Peace)
duas: (The Messenger of Allah said: ‘You shall not enter paradise until you believe, and you shall not believe until you love one another. Shall I not inform you of something, if you were to act upon it, you will indeed achiev
(Aammar said: ‘Three characteristics, whoever combines them, has completed his faith: to be just, to spread greetings to all people and to spend (charitably) out of the little you have.)
(Aabdullah Ibn Aamr reported that a man asked the Prophet : ‘Which Islam is the best?’. He replied: Feed (the poor), and greet those whom you know as well as those whom you do not.)

title: How to reply to a disbeliever if he says Salam to you
duas: (When the people of the Book greet you, reply by saying: (And upon you.))

title: Invocation upon hearing the cock's crow or the bray of a donkey
duas: (If you hear the crow of a rooster, ask Allah for his bounty for it has seen an angel and if you hear the braying of an ass, seek refuge in Allah for it has seen a devil.)

title: Invocation upon hearing a dog barking in the night
duas: (If you hear the barking of dogs or the braying of asses at night, seek refuge in Allah for they see what you do not.)

title: Invocation for someone you have spoken ill to
duas: (O Allah, to any believer whom I have insulted, let that be cause to draw him near to You on the Day of Resurrection.)

title: How a Muslim should praise another Muslim
duas: (He said: ‘If anyone of you is impelled to praise his brother, then he should say: ‘I deem so-and-so to be…and Allah is his reckoner…and I don’t praise anyone, putting it (i.e. my praising) forward, in front of Allah’s c

title: What a Muslim should say when he is praised
duas: O Allah, do not call me to account for what they say and forgive me for what they have no knowledge of [and make me better than they imagine].

title: The pilgrim's announcement of his arrival for Hajj or Umrah
duas: (Here I am O Allah, (in response to Your call), here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.)

title: Saying Allahu Akbar when passing the Black Stone
duas: (The Prophet circled the KaAAbah on a camel, every time he reached the black stone he would point to it with his staff and say: (Allah is the greatest))

title: Invocation to be recited between the Yemenite Corner and the Black Stone
duas: The Prophet PBUH used to say between the Yemeni corner and the black stone: (O our Lord, grant us the best in this life and the best in the next life, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.)

title: Invocation to be recited while standing at Safa and Marwah
duas: (Jabir said when describing the Prophet’s pilgrimage: ‘…and when he approached mount Safa he recited: (Indeed Safa and Marwah are from the places of worship of Allah…) (I begin with what Allah began with.) so he started

title: Invocation to be recited on the Day of Arafat
duas: (The best of supplications is the supplication on the day of AAarafah and the best which I and the Prophets before me have said (is): (None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belo

title: Supplication to be recited at the sacred area of Muzdalifah
duas: The Prophet rode his camel, Al-Qaswa, until he reached the sacred area (Al-Mash aril Haraam). Then he faced the Qiblah and invoked Allah, and repeatedly said the words: Allaahu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great), Allaahu Ah

title: Saying Allahu Akbar while stoning the three pillars at Mina
duas: The Prophet PBUH said Allaahu 'Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) with each pebble he threw at the three pillars. Then he went forward, stood facing the Qiblah and raised his hands and called upon Allah. That was after (sto

title: What to say when surprised or startled
duas: (How perfect Allah is.)
(Allah is the greatest.)

title: What to say when something that pleases you happens
duas: (The Prophet PBUH would prostrate in gratitude to Allah upon receiving news which pleased him or which caused pleasure. )

title: What to say when you feel a pain in your body
duas: (Place your hand at the site of the pain and say: (In the name of Allah(three times)) the supplicate seven times: (I take refuge in Allah and within His omnipotence from the evil that I feel and am wary of.))

title: What to say when you fear you may afflict something with the evil eye
duas: If you see anything of your brother that pleases you, or of his person or of his property [then ask Allah to bless him in it] for the envious eye is real.

title: What to say when you feel frightened
duas: (None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.)

title: What to say when slaughtering or sacrificing an animal
duas: (In the name of Allah, and Allah is the greatest. O Allah, (it is) from You and belongs to You, O Allah, accept this from me.)

title: What to say to foil the devil's plots
duas: (I take refuge within Allah’s perfect words which no righteous or unrighteous person can transgress, from all the evil that He has created, made and originated. (I take refuge) from the evil that descends from the sky an

title: Repentance and seeking forgiveness
duas: (The Messenger of Allah said: ‘By Allah, I seek forgiveness and repent to Allah, more than seventy times a day.)
(He also said: ‘O People, Repent! Verily I repent to Allah, a hundred times a day.)

(He also said: ‘Whoever says:(I seek Allah’s forgiveness, besides whom, none has the right to be worshipped except He, The Ever Living, The Self-Subsisting and Supporter of all, and I turn to Him in repentance.) Allah wo
(He said: ‘The nearest the Lord comes to His servant is in the middle of the night, so if you are able to be of those who remember Allah at that time, then be so.)
(He also said: ‘The nearest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so supplicate much therein.)

(He also said: ‘verily my heart becomes preoccupied, and verily I seek Allah’s forgiveness a hundred times a day.)(preoccupied: i.e. in a state of ‘forgetfulness’. The Prophet always used to increase in his remembrance o

title: The excellence of remembering Allah
duas: (Whoever says:(How perfect Allah is and I praise Him.) a hundred times during the day, his sins are wiped away, even if they are like the foam of the sea.)

title: How the Prophet glorified Allah
duas: (Tasbeeh, it means here, to say: (Subhanal-lah, alhamdu lillah, Allahu akbar.)) (AAabdullah Ibn AAamr said: ’I saw the prophet make tasbeeh with his right hand.)

title: Types of goodness and good etiquette for community life
